brief:
"NAZA," a documentary examining Israel's conduct in Gaza, received the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival, Al Jazeera English reported. The award recognizes the film's artistic and journalistic treatment of the subject at the prestigious international cinema event held annually in Italy.

The prize marks a significant moment for documentary work focused on the Gaza conflict to gain recognition at a major film festival platform. Venice, one of the world's oldest and most prominent film competitions, draws submissions and attendees from across the global cinema industry. The Special Jury Prize places the film among the festival's most honored works alongside its top prizes.
dek: ‘NAZA’, a documentary about Israel’s genocide in Gaza, has won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival.
title: Gaza genocide documentary wins Venice Film Festival's Special Jury Prize
